back: `${expr}` interpolates a value. `%{ if }`/`%{ for }` are directives. `~` trims adjacent whitespace. Escape literals as `$${` and `%%{`.
Square brackets produce a list/tuple; braces produce a map/object (`k => v`). Add `if cond` to filter and `...` after the value to group duplicates into lists.
Works on lists (count resources). For for_each resources (maps) use `values(res)[*].attr` or a `for` expression.
`try(a, b)` returns the first expression that evaluates without error. `can(expr)` returns true/false for whether it evaluates. `can` is mostly for validations.
Build a list of lists of objects with nested `for`, `flatten` it, then key it: `{ for o in local.flat : o.key => o }` for `for_each`.
`"10.0.2.0/24"`: add 8 bits to the prefix and take network number 2.
count: instances by index; good for on/off (`var.x ? 1 : 0`). for_each: instances by key from a map or set of strings; stable when items are added/removed. Default to for_each.
With count over a list, removing an item shifts later indices, so Terraform replaces or destroys the wrong objects. Fix: for_each with stable keys, migrated with moved blocks.

front: Requirement on for_each keys and count
back: Must be known at plan time. Don't derive them from provider-computed attributes (IDs, random values).
`dynamic "ports" { for_each = ...  iterator = p  content { internal = p.value.internal } }`. Generates repeated nested blocks; default iterator name = block label.
`create_before_destroy`, `prevent_destroy`, `ignore_changes`, `replace_triggered_by`, plus `precondition` and `postcondition` blocks. Values must be literals (no variables).
Built-in resource (1.4+) replacing `null_resource`. Holds `input`/`output`, can be replaced via `triggers_replace`, bridges variables into `replace_triggered_by`, hosts provisioners.

front: validation vs precondition vs postcondition vs check
back: validation: inputs (error). precondition: assumptions before acting (error). postcondition: guarantees after acting, uses `self` (error). check: ongoing health, top-level (warning).
`provider "aws" { alias = "use1"  region = "us-east-1" }` then `provider = aws.use1` in a resource. Modules receive them via `providers = { ... }`.
